answer: An agent network can make each identity earn a persistent reputation by completing randomly assigned, cross-checked tasks, with scores tied to a costly stake that is forfeited when peers verify fraud. New identities start with no history, so splitting one agent into many does not multiply trust; each must independently build a record and lock up capital. The kernel enforces the same rules for every account, whether it operates on a tundra route or at a ledge, making a Sybil campaign expensive in both funds and time.
